clue.text: After break, back in a jiffy

indicators.note: the first word sets the order: what follows the break comes after it in the answer

parts.note: to split is to break apart
to second a motion is to back or support it

explanation.surface: Someone promises they will be back very soon after a short break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back in a jiffy' reads as a promise to return, but 'back' is a verb meaning support and 'in' just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiffy and a split second are both idioms for an extremely brief moment of time.

clue.text: Breaking stick?

parts.note: surface reading: a stick that is snapping, or one used to smash something
setter's reading: a break is the opening shot in a game played on a green baize table

explanation.walkthrough: In snooker-type games the 'break' is the first shot that scatters the racked balls, so the stick used for it is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool cue is the long tapered rod players strike the balls with, including on the opening break.

clue.text: Currently doing well, insect in grass

parts.note: a player playing well at present is 'in form'
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A thriving insect is found living in the grass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grass' is British slang for someone who tells the police about criminals, not the lawn plant.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is a police informer, someone who betrays associates to the authorities.

clue.text: A little quarrel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a small piece or amount
second meaning: a fight or squabble

explanation.surface: Just a minor squabble, nothing serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrap means both a tiny fragment of something and, informally, a brief fight or row.

clue.text: Bread I knock over after tea

indicators.note: the tea word goes first and the rest follows it in sequence

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea

indicators.note: knocking something over tips it upside down, which in a down entry turns the letters round

parts.note: taken as written
a tap is a light knock

explanation.surface: Someone clumsily topples a loaf after having a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A chapati is a flat unleavened bread from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Salt last of cheese pie at home, served up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up means reading it from the bottom
only the final letter of the following word is wanted

parts.note: the final letter of cheese
a tart is a pastry pie
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A cook serves up a salty cheese pie at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' reads as seasoning for the pie but is the chemistry sense: a compound formed from an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical salt of nitric acid, such as saltpetre.

clue.text: Shock seeing fat animal eating every other bit of frog

parts.note: flab is excess body fat

indicators.note: something eating something else takes it inside itself

parts.note: a beast is an animal

indicators.note: taking every other bit means keeping alternate letters, here the second and fourth

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of frog

explanation.surface: Someone is horrified to see a fat creature devouring bits of a frog.
explanation.definitionFit: To flabbergast is to astonish or stun someone, a verb matching 'shock' in sense.

clue.text: Geographical plan spread out showing African capital

indicators.note: spreading things around moves them out of their original arrangement

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
the word itself, rearranged

explanation.surface: An atlas page laid open displays a city in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread out' looks like one phrase describing the map, but 'spread' alone signals the shuffle of the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Maputo is the capital city of Mozambique, on the south-east coast of Africa.

clue.text: Start positioning shed behind meadow

indicators.note: one part sits behind, so after, the other in the answer

parts.note: lea is a poetic word for a meadow
to doff is to take off or shed a garment

explanation.surface: A farmer begins by siting a shed at the back of a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like a garden building but is a verb, as in shedding clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead off is to begin or open proceedings, so it can stand in for 'start'.

clue.text: Venetian bridge tailor-made?

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, reworked from their printed order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Asks whether a famous bridge in Venice was custom-built to order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailor-made' reads as one hyphenated word; split it and the first half is the letters, the second the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the oldest and best-known bridge crossing the Grand Canal in Venice.

clue.text: Blue chatter I edited in article

indicators.note: the reworked letters go inside the word that follows

parts.note: the definite article

indicators.note: edited text has been reworked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some rude gossip has been cut out of a newspaper piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' looks like 'risqué' describing the chatter, but in British politics blue is the Conservative colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A Thatcherite, follower of Margaret Thatcher, is a Conservative, and Tories are called blues after their party colour.

clue.text: Heavy trampolinist?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a heavy is a burly doorman or minder
second meaning, whimsical: someone who bounces

explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy' looks like an adjective, but it is the noun for a hired strongman; the question mark flags the playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouncer is a nightclub doorman, a heavy, and literally anyone who bounces, like a trampolinist.

clue.text: Husband held by soldier: gosh mummy!

indicators.note: something held by another sits within its grasp, so inside it

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper
H is the abbreviation for husband
an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A child exclaims at a husband being arrested by a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mummy' reads as a child calling to mother, but it is an embalmed body from ancient Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Many Egyptian kings were preserved as mummies, so a pharaoh is an example of a mummy.

clue.text: In retirement, English and Central European run away together

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
a Pole comes from Poland in central Europe

explanation.surface: An English and a Polish pensioner run off together in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: To elope is for a couple to run off secretly to marry.

clue.text: Missing drinking container of beer? Certainly!

definitions.text: Missing drinking container of beer? Certainly!

indicators.note: someone drinking takes something into themselves, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: missing means absent
beer can come in a tin

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether you are going without a can of beer, and gets a firm yes.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes someone who certainly goes without beer; 'Certainly!' confirms the description rather than giving letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Being abstinent means refraining from alcohol, so such a person certainly misses out on the beer.

clue.text: Funny turn before dance

indicators.note: one part comes before the other in the finished word

parts.note: to screw is to turn, as with a screw
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A comedian does a funny routine before a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Funny turn' reads as a comic act or a dizzy spell, but the definition is 'Funny' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwball is an adjective for zany, eccentric comedy, as in screwball films.

clue.text: Large tank has me kept in storage when explosive

indicators.note: something kept in another is placed inside it
an explosion scatters things, so the letters land in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A huge tank holds the speaker in storage when it is about to blow up.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a big cylindrical holder for storing town gas, an example of a large tank.

clue.text: As rising, heading for breakfast and wash, time for rest

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of breakfast
a bath is a wash

explanation.surface: A morning routine of getting up, breakfast and a wash before a day off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of religious rest, a time set aside for not working.

clue.text: Test revolutionary citric substance in lemon, on having been cut

indicators.note: a revolution turns things round, so the whole result is read backwards
the substance goes inside the fruit word
cutting something removes it, so the named letters are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed
citric acid is found in citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A test of a radical citric compound on a lemon that has been sliced.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the second word from the fruit, slip the acid in after its first letter, then turn everything round.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical is a physical examination, so as a noun it means a health test.

clue.text: Twin fixture

definitions.meaning: first meaning: as a verb, to pair or equal
second meaning: a scheduled sporting game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Twin fixture' sounds like a double-header, but it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: To match is to pair one thing with its equal, and a match is a sports fixture.

clue.text: Watch car touring Northern Ireland

indicators.note: a vehicle touring a region goes all around it, enclosing it

parts.note: a motor is a car
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone observes a car driving around Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: To monitor something is to keep it under observation, a synonym of the verb watch.

clue.text: A consumable computer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a pill that is swallowed
second meaning: a flat touchscreen computing device

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark invites a picture of an edible computer; really it is two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is both a pill taken as medicine and a slim handheld touchscreen computer.

clue.text: Item of furniture found in case, correct

indicators.note: something found in another sits inside it

parts.note: a suit is a legal case
a bed is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture turns up packed in a suitcase, which is right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' suggests luggage but means a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to correct and prepare copy for publication, as a newspaper sub-editor does.

clue.text: 'Hair': appearing in theatres Saturday

indicators.note: the letters appear inside the words that follow, spanning them

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of one word and start of the next

explanation.surface: The musical Hair is playing in theatres on Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks make 'Hair' look like the 1960s rock musical's title, but it is the plain word.
explanation.definitionFit: A tress is a long lock of hair, so the singular noun matches 'hair'.

clue.text: Special brew in a pub

indicators.note: something special is made out of the ordinary, so the letters take an unusual new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A special beer is on tap at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine bar is a drinking establishment, a near relative of the pub that specialises in wine.

clue.text: Awkward, left in Marseille?

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the French word for left, as spoken in a French city

explanation.walkthrough: Marseille is a French port, so 'left' there is said in French; English borrowed that same word for clumsiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauche means socially awkward in English and is the French word for the left-hand side.

clue.text: A way to maintain performance of rite, most creative

indicators.note: to maintain is to hold or support, so the outer letters keep the rest inside

parts.note: A taken as written plus ST, short for street

indicators.note: a performance is a new rendering, so the word is played in a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A ritual is performed in the most inventive way possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Artiest is the superlative of arty, meaning showily artistic or creative.

clue.text: Fresh sole caught by fishermen, traders in large quantities

indicators.note: something caught by another ends up held inside it

parts.note: whalers hunt at sea, a loose sense of fishermen

indicators.note: a fresh version is newly made, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Fishermen land fresh sole and sell it to bulk traders.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholesalers buy and sell goods in bulk, chiefly to retailers rather than the public.
